domain_label: Sweater Manufacturing — Minimum Batch, Working Capital & Volume Scaling Economics
purpose: A method for sizing the binding minimum batch, the launch first-cheque, and the working-capital cash trap behind an apparently-profitable ex-factory sweater cost, and for reading how that cost falls in steps with volume: establishing that the binding minimum is dye-lot MOQ (not garment/CMT MOQ), that per-style setup amortised over a tiny MOQ pushes true micro-volume cost above the published conversion bands, that cash leaves months before it returns, that the make-vs-buy crossover is governed by the [UNKNOWN] Ludhiana per-piece job-work rate, and that every money/MOQ/throughput figure is expressed strictly as a labelled [ESTIMATE] (band, never fake-precise), a cited [FACT], or a named [UNKNOWN] blocker, then handed cleanly to the T9 landed-cost P&L.
assumptions: this KB computes ex-factory conversion cost, minimum batch, and the cash tied up before revenue; it is explicitly not landed cost, not COGS-to-stock, and not a P&L, all of which live in T9

no live mandi, dyer, or job-worker quote stands behind any figure; every cost/price/throughput/MOQ figure is a labelled [ESTIMATE] band with method and confidence, a cited [FACT], or a named [UNKNOWN]

the single highest-leverage missing number is the Ludhiana per-piece knit + LINK job-work rate, held [UNKNOWN] and named as the blocker that gates both band precision and the make-vs-buy crossover; it is never fabricated

the base case is an acrylic + acrylic-blend Ludhiana cluster with three articles (A1 cotton-blend core, A2 fine-acrylic value, A3 merino/lambswool premium) sourced into the job-work mesh on bought-dyed stock-shade yarn
yarn is well-anchored at ~50-60% of the knit-garment stack and sets the level of the cost; the [UNKNOWN] knit + LINK rate sets the uncertainty; effort belongs on the rate, not on cheaper yarn

off-paper friction/'speed-money' and inverted-duty/GST drag are real but not clean per-garment COGS adds; they are named as mechanism and cash-cycle cost respectively, with amounts [UNKNOWN] by design and routed to T9

the make-vs-buy verdict (buy at launch, graduate to making only on sustained single-program volume, linking last, dyehouse and machine-building never) is reconstructed-consensus from T1/T2/T3, later stress-tested by an adversarial analyst-B; the cost view here is consistent with it but the crossover stays blocked by the [UNKNOWN] rate
exclusions: ocean freight, US duty (cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5% / wool 6110.11 ~16% / acrylic-MMF 6110.30.30 ~32%), insurance, broker, drayage, and import financing — the landed-cost stack owned by T9
CAC, returns, payment fees, AOV, and contribution-margin-after-CAC — the D2C viability test owned by T7/T9, which decides whether the venture makes money
machine selection, used-machine landed quotes, and own-line capacity engineering detail — owned by the T3 machines specialist
yarn count/fibre/blend specification and dyeing-stage QC detail — owned by the T2 yarn specialist
linking-seam, anti-pill, and AQL inspection execution detail — owned by the T5 quality and T6 finishing specialists
any fabricated point value for the [UNKNOWN] Ludhiana per-piece knit/LINK rate, the friction/speed-money magnitude, or the inverted-duty drag magnitude
source_description: labelled [ESTIMATE] bands, cited [FACT] anchors, and named [UNKNOWN] blockers for the sweater batch-and-capital model, grounded in the manufacturing-economics deep-dive (DEEPDIVE.md), its adversarial make-vs-buy challenge (analyst_b_make_vs_buy.md), and the upstream Ludhiana, yarn, and machines deep-dives; conversion-cost shape uses a published fully-fashioned-knitwear costing study, yarn-share uses the Vardhman FY20 raw-material anchor, dye-lot MOQ and lead-time use the yarn deep-dive, and duty/HTS use USITC
source_citation: Vardhman FY20 raw material = 54% of revenue (T1 yarn-share anchor); published FF-knitwear conversion study (knitting ~US$0.74/pc, linking ~US$0.45/pc, finishing chain ~US$0.7-1.0/pc, shape only, not a Ludhiana quote); Punjab minimum wage floor ~Rs438/day (~US$5.1); dye-house economic MOQ ~500-2,000 kg/colour with a +20-50% small-batch surcharge below it (T2 yarn deep-dive); garment/CMT MOQ ~100-300 pcs/style-colour (T2); yarn-in to goods-ready ~6-12 weeks (T2); USITC HTS heading 6110 (cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5%, wool 6110.11 ~16%, acrylic/MMF 6110.30.30 ~32%); USD/INR ~Rs83/$; mfg_economics DEEPDIVE.md, analyst_b_make_vs_buy.md, ludhiana/yarn/machines DEEPDIVE.md

competency_questions.question: What exactly is the cost this KB computes, and what four numbers is it explicitly NOT, so a profitable ex-factory figure is never mistaken for landed cost or a P&L?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COST_BOUNDARY_FRAME states the model is ex-factory conversion cost and is not landed cost, not COGS-to-stock, not a P&L, and not a live quote, routing each excluded number to T9 or T7/T9 and tagging the boundary [FACT] on identities

competency_questions.question: Why does yarn set the LEVEL of the cost while the knit + LINK job-work rate sets the UNCERTAINTY, and what does that imply for where effort goes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TWO_NUMBER_FRAME ties yarn to ~50-60% of the stack ([ESTIMATE] from the 54% Vardhman anchor) and the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate to ~25-45% of the conversion subtotal, concluding effort belongs on the rate not on cheaper yarn

competency_questions.question: What is the single highest-leverage missing number, why does it stay [UNKNOWN], and what does acquiring it unblock?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: JOBWORK_RATE_BLOCKER names the Rs/piece knit + LINK rate as [UNKNOWN] with no reliable public figure, forbids fabrication, and states one quote run halves every band and locates the make-vs-buy crossover

competency_questions.question: Why is dye-lot MOQ, not garment/CMT MOQ, the binding minimum batch, and how does it make the launch colour-starved rather than style-starved?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DYE_LOT_MOQ gives the ~150-500 kg/colour binding floor ([ESTIMATE], surcharge below dye-house ~500-2,000 kg economic MOQ), converts ~200 kg to ~500-650 sweaters of one colour, and concludes ~2-4 launch colours, colour-starved not style-starved

competency_questions.question: How does garment/CMT MOQ sit as the smaller constraint beneath the dye lot, and what is its band?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GARMENT_CMT_MOQ states the ~100-300 pcs/style-colour band ([ESTIMATE, MED]) and explains the dye lot forces cash commitment for 500+ pieces of a colour whether or not demand exists

competency_questions.question: Why do per-style setup costs (PPS, tech-pack, lab dips, AQL) amortised over a tiny MOQ push true micro cost ABOVE the published conversion bands?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PER_STYLE_SETUP states setup is per-style spread over the run ([ESTIMATE, LOW], ~$300-1,500/style basis), shows a 150-piece run adds a meaningful per-garment uplift that nearly vanishes at 1,000 pieces, and flags this as why the bands understate launch cost

competency_questions.question: How is the per-article ex-factory conversion band built so it stays an honest labelled illustration and is blocked at exactly one input?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONVERSION_STACK_BANDS gives the A1 ~$4-9 / A2 ~$3.5-8 / A3 ~$6-22+ bands as [ESTIMATE] illustrations, names the published study as shape-only (not a Ludhiana quote), and marks the knit+LINK lines [UNKNOWN] as the blocked input

competency_questions.question: By how much does true micro-volume cost sit above the conversion bands once the setup uplift and the small-batch dye surcharge stack?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MICRO_COST_UPLIFT states the setup uplift plus the +20-50%/colour dye surcharge push true 150-piece cost to ~1.3-2x the band midpoint ([ESTIMATE, LOW], illustrative multiplier), and names the MOQ/setup figures as the blockers

competency_questions.question: What is the owner's real launch first-cheque, and how is it composed so it is the number that sizes the runway rather than the unit cost?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LAUNCH_FIRST_CHEQUE recomputes first_cheque = dyed-yarn MOQ value (2-4 colours) + per-style setup (3 articles) + conversion on 500-1,500 pieces + the cash tied for the cycle, expressed as a few-lakh-rupee [ESTIMATE, LOW-MED] blocked by the [UNKNOWN] dye MOQ and job-work rate

competency_questions.question: Why is the working-capital trap, not the unit cost, the killer, given cash leaves months before it returns?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WORKING_CAPITAL_TRAP states yarn-in to goods-ready is ~6-12 weeks ([ESTIMATE, MED]) before ocean and sell-through add more, framing the whole cash-conversion cycle as a long front-loaded cash-out that a profitable-on-paper sweater hides

competency_questions.question: How does the winter-weighted seasonal calendar amplify the cash trap, and why must the launch avoid the Jul-Oct cluster peak?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEASONAL_CASH_TIMING explains committing a launch drop into the Jul-Oct peak stretches lead time and working capital exactly when least affordable, and states the rule do not launch into the peak

competency_questions.question: Why is the inverted-duty / GST drag a cash-cycle cost rather than a per-garment COGS add, and which article does it bite?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INVERTED_DUTY_DRAG states acrylic/MMF inputs taxed above output trap working capital in slow refunds ([FACT]), bites A2 specifically, holds the magnitude [UNKNOWN], and routes it to T9 as a cash-cycle line not a COGS add

competency_questions.question: Why does unit cost fall in STEPS rather than smoothly as volume rises, and what are the two threshold channels?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VOLUME_STEP_CURVE names the two fixed/threshold channels (clearing the dye-lot economic MOQ surcharge, and amortising per-style setup) and concludes the per-garment cost drops in steps, the first step being the ~500 kg/colour dye MOQ

competency_questions.question: How is a launch go/no-go reached, what blocker gates the make-vs-buy crossover, and how are the batch and cash reads refreshed when the quote run lands?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LAUNCH_GO_NOGO composes the micro-cost uplift, the cash trap, the seasonal timing, and the make-vs-buy crossover (gated by JOBWORK_RATE_BLOCKER) into a verdict refusing a peak-timed or cash-starved launch, and BATCH_REVIEW_LOOP defines the refresh triggers (a job-work/FOB quote run, a named dye MOQ, live yarn prices, a T9 landed-input or duty-rate change) that re-run the first cheque and the bands

glossary.definition: The cost this KB computes: full (dyed) yarn + knit job-work + LINK job-work + finishing + trims/labels/pack + compliance loading on the labour-bearing portion + job-worker margin, ending at the factory gate; explicitly not landed cost, not COGS-to-stock, and not a P&L, all of which are T9/T7's.

The smallest run the venture is forced to commit, set not by the garment but by the dye-lot MOQ (~150-500 kg of dyed yarn per colour); at ~300-400 g/sweater this is ~500-650 sweaters of one colour, so the launch is colour-starved (2-4 colours) rather than style-starved.

A +20-50% per-colour premium charged when a dye lot sits below the dye-house economic MOQ (~500-2,000 kg/colour); a threshold cost that disappears once a colour clears economic MOQ, and the first step on the volume cost curve.

The per-style fixed costs (sampling/PPS proto-fit-PP, tech-pack, lab dips, AQL inspection setup) spread over a run; over a 150-piece run they add a meaningful per-garment uplift, over a 1,000-piece run they nearly vanish, which is why the published conversion bands understate true micro-volume cost.

glossary.term: true micro cost above the bands
glossary.definition: The fact that at the smallest MOQ the per-style setup uplift plus the small-batch dye surcharge push real ex-factory cost to ~1.3-2x the conversion-band midpoint, so the published bands are a variable-stack floor, not the launch cost.

The owner's real opening commitment = dyed-yarn MOQ value for 2-4 colours + per-style setup for 3 articles + knit/link/finish on 500-1,500 pieces + months of that cash tied up; an [ESTIMATE, LOW-MED] of a few lakh rupees blocked by the [UNKNOWN] dye MOQ and job-work rate, and the number that sizes the runway, not the unit cost.

The killer the unit cost hides: cash leaves to buy/dye/knit/link/finish (~6-12 weeks yarn-in to goods-ready) then ships and sells before it returns, so the whole cash-conversion cycle is a long front-loaded cash-out that can bankrupt a profitable-on-paper brand.

Acrylic (MMF) inputs taxed higher than the output trapping working capital in slow refunds; a [FACT] mechanism that bites A2, with magnitude [UNKNOWN], expressed as a T9 cash-cycle cost rather than a per-garment COGS add.

The shape of per-garment cost as volume rises: it drops in steps, not smoothly, through two fixed/threshold channels - clearing the dye-lot economic MOQ surcharge (first step) and amortising per-style setup (second step) - with owning knitting only at sustained single-program volume.

The volume at which owned per-piece cost (machine + programmer + operator + power + linker, divided by pieces actually run) undercuts the subcontract per-piece rate; entirely governed by the [UNKNOWN] Ludhiana job-work rate, so it cannot be located until that rate is quoted - the same missing number that sets band precision.

nodes.definition: Fix the boundary before any number: this KB computes ex-factory conversion cost per garment (full dyed yarn + knit job-work + LINK job-work + finishing + trims/labels/pack + compliance loading on the labour-bearing portion + job-worker margin), ending at the factory gate. It is explicitly NOT four other numbers: not landed cost (ocean freight, US duty cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5% / wool 6110.11 ~16% / acrylic-MMF 6110.30.30 ~32% [FACT-USITC], insurance, broker, drayage, financing all live in T9), not COGS-to-stock, not a P&L (CAC, returns, fees, AOV, and contribution-margin-after-CAC are the T7/T9 survival test), and not a live quote (bands only, by honest necessity). Getting the boundary wrong is the most expensive mistake in the segment, so it comes first.

included: the four numbers it is not
routing each excluded number to T9 or T7/T9
excluded: the per-article band values (their own node)

pros.claim: Fixing the boundary first stops a cheap factory-gate number being read as landed cost or a P&L
pros.example: a $5 ex-factory sweater is not a $5 delivered or $5-margin sweater once duty and CAC are added downstream

cons.claim: A hard boundary can read as evasive to a reader who wants one all-in number
cons.example: an owner asking 'what does it cost to sell' is deferred to T9 rather than answered here

failure_modes: reading the ex-factory figure as a landed or COGS-to-stock number
over-optimising the factory gate when the margin fight is downstream in T7/T9
acceptance_tests: the model is stated as ex-factory conversion cost and explicitly distinguished from landed cost, COGS-to-stock, a P&L, and a live quote, with each excluded number routed to T9 or T7/T9
revisit_triggers: T9 changes the landed-stack composition
a new compliance or duty line shifts what belongs inside vs outside the gate
an owner request conflates ex-factory with delivered cost

base.update_signal: the landed-stack composition or the inside-vs-outside-gate line changes

nodes.definition: Reduce the segment to two facts pulling opposite ways. Yarn sets the LEVEL and is well-anchored: ~50-60% of the knit-garment stack ([ESTIMATE, MED] from the Vardhman FY20 raw-material = 54%-of-revenue anchor, held not promoted to a measured cluster average), ~$1-2.50 of fibre per value/core sweater at ~300-500 g. The job-work rate sets the UNCERTAINTY and is [UNKNOWN]: knit + LINK labour is ~25-45% of the conversion subtotal with no reliable public per-piece figure. The owner takeaway: do not hunt cheaper yarn (small, anchored, not the constraint); spend effort getting the one Rs/piece rate, because it both halves every band and settles the make-vs-buy decision.

included: the knit+LINK rate as the uncertainty (~25-45%)
excluded: the [UNKNOWN] rate's blocker status (its own node)

pros.claim: Splitting level from uncertainty tells the owner where effort actually pays
pros.example: chasing a 5% cheaper yarn moves the stack less than pinning the rate that halves every band

cons.claim: The 50-60% yarn share is a single-anchor estimate, not a measured cluster average
cons.example: a fibre-mix or count change could move the share outside the band for a given article

failure_modes: promoting the 54% Vardhman anchor to a measured cluster fact
spending optimisation effort on yarn rather than on the rate that sets uncertainty
acceptance_tests: yarn is tied to ~50-60% of the stack as an [ESTIMATE] from the 54% anchor and the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate to ~25-45% of the conversion subtotal, with the effort-on-the-rate conclusion stated
revisit_triggers: a measured cluster yarn-share figure replaces the single anchor
a live job-work rate quote lands and changes the uncertainty width
a fibre/count shift moves the yarn share

base.update_signal: the yarn-share anchor or the job-work-rate uncertainty changes

nodes.definition: Name the single highest-leverage missing number and hold it [UNKNOWN]: the Ludhiana per-piece knit + LINK job-work rate (Rs/piece at 7GG and 12GG, for 300 g and 400 g pullovers) has no reliable public figure, confirmed across the upstream open questions and a fresh search. Those two lines are ~25-45% of the conversion subtotal - the part that cannot be priced. We do not invent it; we bound it with a labelled external cross-check (a published FF-knitwear study: knitting ~$0.74/pc, linking ~$0.45/pc, finishing ~$0.7-1.0/pc, shape only) and call the result an illustration. One on-the-ground quote run from 2-3 job-workers collapses it to [ESTIMATE, MED], tightens every band by ~half, and locates the make-vs-buy crossover - the single highest-leverage data acquisition in the segment.

excluded: the make-vs-buy crossover computation (its own node)

pros.claim: Holding the rate [UNKNOWN] and naming it as THE blocker prevents a fabricated precision the whole model would inherit
pros.example: refusing to harden loose trade fragments into a quotable rate keeps the bands honest

cons.claim: An [UNKNOWN] at the core limits how decisively any downstream band or crossover can be stated
cons.example: a reader wanting a single ex-factory number is left with a ~half-width band until the quote run

failure_modes: fabricating a point rate from loose trade fragments to win an argument
treating the published-study cross-check as a Ludhiana quote rather than a shape illustration
acceptance_tests: the knit+LINK Rs/piece rate is held [UNKNOWN] with no reliable public figure, the external study is labelled shape-only, fabrication is forbidden, and one quote run is named as halving the bands and locating the crossover
revisit_triggers: a real job-work quote run from 2-3 named units lands
a credible published Ludhiana per-piece rate appears
a productivity (pc/operator-day) figure for Ludhiana becomes available

base.update_signal: a job-work-rate quote run or a Ludhiana productivity figure lands

nodes.definition: Establish the binding minimum batch: it is set by dye-lot MOQ, not by the garment. The binding number is ~150-500 kg of dyed yarn per colour ([ESTIMATE]; dye-house economic MOQ ~500-2,000 kg/colour with a +20-50% small-batch surcharge below it; floor MED-HIGH, exact kg at a named dyer [UNKNOWN]). At ~300-400 g/sweater, ~200 kg is ~500-650 sweaters of ONE colour. So the launch line is colour-starved, not style-starved: plan only ~2-4 launch colours across all three articles, share dye lots across styles, and reserve a proven hero colour before paying surcharges or graduating to job-work dyeing. The dye lot is what forces a cash commitment for 500+ pieces of a colour whether or not demand exists.

excluded: the small-batch surcharge as a volume step (scaling node)

pros.claim: Identifying dye-lot MOQ as the binding minimum reframes the launch around colour count, not style count
pros.example: 200 kg = ~500-650 sweaters of one colour forces 2-4 colours regardless of how many styles are designed

cons.claim: The exact kg floor is dyer-specific and stale, so the band is wide until a named dyer quotes
cons.example: a dyer with a lower economic MOQ would loosen the 2-4-colour constraint

failure_modes: sizing the launch by garment MOQ and under-buying yarn for a colour
designing many colours against a dye-lot floor that forces over-buying or surcharges
acceptance_tests: dye-lot MOQ is stated as the ~150-500 kg/colour binding minimum ([ESTIMATE]), converted to ~500-650 sweaters/colour, and tied to a ~2-4 launch-colour, colour-starved-not-style-starved conclusion
revisit_triggers: a named Ludhiana dyer quotes a real lot MOQ and surcharge
a yarn weight-per-garment assumption changes the kg-to-sweaters math
a hero colour is proven and shifts the colour plan

base.update_signal: a named dyer's lot MOQ or surcharge becomes available

nodes.definition: Place the garment/CMT MOQ as the smaller constraint beneath the dye lot. Small Ludhiana units accept ~100-300 pcs per style-colour ([ESTIMATE, MED]) for cut-make-trim-link work. This is real but smaller than the dye-lot floor: the dye lot forces cash commitment for 500+ pieces of a colour, so the garment MOQ rarely binds first. The interaction matters for SKU planning - a 3-style x 3-colour capsule is 9 style-colours, each clearing its own ~100-300 pc CMT MOQ, but all drawing from only 2-4 shared dye lots, so the colour count, not the style or CMT count, sets the cash floor.

included: why it sits beneath the dye lot
excluded: the dye-lot binding floor (its own node)

pros.claim: Ranking CMT MOQ below the dye lot stops the smaller constraint being mistaken for the binding one
pros.example: a 150-pc CMT-feasible style still needs 500+ pieces of its colour bought as yarn

cons.claim: The CMT MOQ band is itself an estimate that varies by unit and construction
cons.example: a fully-fashioned style may carry a higher minimum than a simple cut-and-sew blank

failure_modes: treating the CMT MOQ as the binding minimum and under-sizing yarn
ignoring that shared dye lots, not per-style CMT minimums, set the cash floor
acceptance_tests: the garment/CMT MOQ is stated as ~100-300 pcs/style-colour ([ESTIMATE, MED]) and explicitly placed as the smaller constraint beneath the dye lot's 500+-piece-per-colour commitment
revisit_triggers: a named CMT unit quotes a real small-run minimum
a construction change (FF vs C&S) shifts the per-style minimum
the capsule SKU matrix changes

base.update_signal: a named unit's small-run CMT MOQ becomes available

nodes.definition: Quantify why per-style fixed costs amortised over a tiny MOQ push true micro cost above the conversion bands. Sampling/PPS (proto-fit-PP), tech-pack, lab dips, and AQL inspection setup are per-style costs spread over the run ([ESTIMATE, LOW]; basis: skilled multi-day tasks at cluster labour rates plus lab-dip and inspection fees, on the order of $300-1,500/style, magnitude [UNKNOWN] at a named unit). Over a 150-piece first run that is roughly +$2-10/garment; over a 1,000-piece run it is ~+$0.30-1.50/garment - nearly vanishing. This is the single biggest reason the conversion bands understate true launch cost: they are the variable conversion stack and carry no amortised setup.

included: why the bands understate launch cost
excluded: the combined micro-volume uplift multiplier (its own node)

pros.claim: Pricing setup over the MOQ exposes a per-garment uplift the variable bands hide
pros.example: $300-1,500 spread over 150 pieces is +$2-10/garment, material at launch scale

cons.claim: The $300-1,500/style basis is an illustrative estimate, not a named-unit quote
cons.example: a unit bundling sampling into the piece price would shift the apparent uplift

failure_modes: reading the conversion bands as the launch cost without adding amortised setup
treating the $300-1,500/style as a quoted fact rather than an [ESTIMATE, LOW] illustration
acceptance_tests: per-style setup is stated as a per-style cost spread over the run ([ESTIMATE, LOW], ~$300-1,500/style basis), with the 150-piece vs 1,000-piece per-garment spread shown and the band-understatement consequence named
revisit_triggers: a named unit quotes real sampling/PPS/tech-pack/lab-dip/AQL setup costs
the launch MOQ changes the amortisation base
an inspection or lab-dip fee schedule updates

base.update_signal: a named-unit per-style setup figure or the amortisation MOQ changes

nodes.definition: Build the three per-article ex-factory conversion bands as labelled illustrations, blocked at exactly one input. Shared assumptions stated so they are reproducible: FF construction subcontracted into the mesh, bought-dyed stock-shade yarn, USD/INR ~Rs83/$, conversion shape from a published FF-knitwear study (knitting ~$0.74/pc, linking ~$0.45/pc, finishing chain ~$0.7-1.0/pc - shape only, NOT a Ludhiana quote), compliance loading +10-15% on the labour-bearing portion only, trims+QC ~$0.8-1.8. The bands: A1 cotton-blend 12-month core ~$4-9/garment; A2 fine-acrylic value driver ~$3.5-8/garment (the floor); A3 merino/lambswool premium ~$6-22+/garment (yarn-dominated, order-of-magnitude). Each is [ESTIMATE, LOW-MED] with the knit+LINK lines marked [UNKNOWN] as the blocked input; loose trade fragments sit inside the band but are consistent, not confirmatory, and are never hardened into a quotable rate.

included: the [UNKNOWN]-rate blocked input and the reproducible assumptions
excluded: the micro-volume uplift over the bands (its own node)

pros.claim: Labelled per-article bands anchored to stated assumptions give a planning estimate without faking a quote
pros.example: A2 ~$3.5-8 as the floor lets a reader audit the band end to end while seeing it is blocked at the rate

cons.claim: The bands rest on a transferred study shape and an [UNKNOWN] rate, so any article can sit far outside its band
cons.example: a cable or fine-12GG A1 runs slower and costlier than the band midpoint

failure_modes: treating a band as a confirmed cost rather than a blocked illustration
hardening loose trade fragments into a quotable rate inside the band
acceptance_tests: each article (A1 ~$4-9, A2 ~$3.5-8, A3 ~$6-22+) has a labelled [ESTIMATE] band with stated assumptions, the study marked shape-only, and the knit+LINK lines flagged [UNKNOWN] as the blocked input
revisit_triggers: the job-work rate quote run lands and tightens the bands
live yarn prices replace stale anchors
an importer quotes the A3 premium tops

base.update_signal: the job-work rate, live yarn prices, or an A3 importer quote changes

nodes.definition: Connect setup and surcharge to show true micro-volume cost sits materially above the conversion bands. The per-style setup uplift (PER_STYLE_SETUP) stacks with the small-batch dye surcharge (+20-50%/colour below dye-house economic MOQ), both hitting the same micro-volume. Method [ESTIMATE, LOW - illustrative arithmetic, not a quote]: over a 150-piece first run the setup uplift can rival or exceed the entire variable conversion cost, so true ex-factory cost can sit plausibly at ~1.3-2x the band midpoint; the multiplier is illustrative and the real number needs the MOQ and setup blockers. This is the buy-verdict's most quantifiable fragility and it is unquantified: it also partly argues for a higher-MOQ full-package option that amortises setup better, but that trade study is blocked by the [UNKNOWN] MOQ.

included: the blockers that gate the real number
excluded: the volume-step recovery of cost (scaling node)

pros.claim: Quantifying the uplift as far as honesty allows stops the bands being read as launch cost
pros.example: a ~1.3-2x multiplier on a 150-piece run reframes A2's $3.5-8 floor as a higher real launch cost

cons.claim: The 1.3-2x multiplier is illustrative and inherits the setup and MOQ uncertainties
cons.example: a unit that bundles setup or a colour that clears economic MOQ would shrink the multiplier

failure_modes: quoting the conversion bands as launch cost and ignoring the uplift
presenting the 1.3-2x multiplier as a measured figure rather than an [ESTIMATE, LOW] illustration
acceptance_tests: the setup uplift and the +20-50% dye surcharge are shown to stack to ~1.3-2x the band midpoint at a 150-piece run ([ESTIMATE, LOW]), with the MOQ and setup figures named as the blockers
revisit_triggers: the per-style setup figure is quoted
the dye-lot MOQ and surcharge are quoted at a named dyer
the launch MOQ changes the amortisation

base.update_signal: the per-style setup or dye-lot surcharge figure changes

nodes.definition: Recompute the owner's real launch first-cheque, which is NOT unit cost x pieces. It is the sum: first_cheque = dyed-yarn MOQ value (for 2-4 colours) + per-style setup (for 3 articles) + knit/link/finish conversion on 500-1,500 pieces + the cash tied up for months before revenue. Worked as a formula: take ~2-4 dye lots at ~150-500 kg/colour priced at the live yarn Rs/kg, add ~3 x per-style setup ($300-1,500 each), add the conversion stack x the committed piece count, then carry that total as tied cash across the ~6-12 week ex-factory cycle plus ocean and sell-through. A sweater costing ~$5 ex-factory still means committing on the order of a few lakh rupees of yarn + setup before the first sale ([ESTIMATE, LOW-MED]; exact figure blocked by the [UNKNOWN] dye MOQ and job-work rate). This, not the unit cost, sizes the launch and the cash runway.

included: the first-cheque formula and its four terms
the [UNKNOWN] blockers on the exact figure

pros.claim: Composing the first cheque as a formula shows the runway-sizing number the unit cost hides
pros.example: dye-MOQ yarn + 3 setups + conversion on 1,000 pieces dwarfs any single unit cost

cons.claim: Two of the formula's terms are blocked, so the total is an order-of-magnitude not a figure
cons.example: without the dye MOQ value and the job-work rate the few-lakh estimate stays a band

failure_modes: sizing the launch as unit cost x pieces and under-funding the runway
presenting the few-lakh figure as precise rather than blocked by the [UNKNOWN] inputs
acceptance_tests: first_cheque is recomputed as dye-yarn MOQ value (2-4 colours) + per-style setup (3 articles) + conversion on 500-1,500 pieces + tied cash, given as a few-lakh-rupee [ESTIMATE, LOW-MED] blocked by the [UNKNOWN] dye MOQ and job-work rate
revisit_triggers: the dye-lot MOQ value is quoted
the job-work rate is quoted
live yarn Rs/kg or the committed piece count changes

base.update_signal: a dye-MOQ value, job-work rate, or live yarn price feeds the formula

nodes.definition: Make the working-capital trap, not the unit cost, the killer the analysis foregrounds. Cash leaves to buy, dye, knit, link, and finish, then ships India to US ocean, then sells, then (for D2C) often collects after returns settle. Yarn-in to goods-ready ex-factory alone is ~6-12 weeks ([ESTIMATE, MED]); ocean plus sell-through plus returns add many more weeks (T9). The whole cash-conversion cycle is a long, front-loaded cash-out: a sweater profitable on paper can still bankrupt a brand because the cash is gone for months before any revenue returns. The unit cost says nothing about this duration; the first cheque x the cycle length is what actually strains the runway.

included: why a profitable unit cost hides it
excluded: the inverted-duty cash drag (its own node)

pros.claim: Foregrounding the cash cycle shows why a profitable unit cost is not solvency
pros.example: a $5 sweater with cash gone for 4-6 months can still drain a thin brand's runway

cons.claim: The 6-12 week ex-factory figure is an estimate and only the first leg of the full cycle
cons.example: ocean and sell-through, owned by T9, dominate the total but are out of scope here

failure_modes: reading a profitable unit cost as solvency and under-funding the cash gap
stopping at the ex-factory 6-12 weeks and ignoring the ocean/sell-through legs T9 owns
acceptance_tests: the cash trap is stated with the ~6-12 week yarn-in-to-goods-ready leg ([ESTIMATE, MED]) plus the ocean/sell-through extension, framing the whole cycle as a front-loaded cash-out the unit cost hides
revisit_triggers: a real ex-factory lead time is observed
T9 supplies the ocean and sell-through legs
a returns-settlement term changes the collection lag

base.update_signal: an observed lead time or the T9 ocean/sell-through legs change the cycle

nodes.definition: Account for how the winter-weighted seasonal calendar amplifies the cash trap. The product is winter-weighted, and committing a launch drop into the Jul-Oct Ludhiana cluster peak stretches lead time AND working capital exactly when the brand can least afford it: the job-workers are full of their big domestic winter clients, a tiny order sits behind them, and the cash is committed longer at the worst moment. The binding rule is do not launch into the peak - phase yarn purchase and conversion ahead of or after the cluster's busy window so the first cheque is not tied up while lead times are longest and queue priority for a micro-account is lowest.

included: the winter-weighted demand and Jul-Oct cluster peak
excluded: the base cash cycle (its own node)

pros.claim: Naming the peak turns the cash trap into a concrete calendar rule
pros.example: phasing the launch outside Jul-Oct shortens the worst-case lead time and tied-cash window

cons.claim: Avoiding the peak collides with hitting the winter selling season on the US side
cons.example: shipping too late to reach the US winter window trades one timing risk for another

failure_modes: committing the launch drop into the Jul-Oct cluster peak
ignoring micro-account queue priority when timing the conversion window
acceptance_tests: the Jul-Oct cluster peak is named as the window that stretches lead time and working capital, with the explicit do-not-launch-into-the-peak rule stated
revisit_triggers: the cluster's seasonal peak window shifts
the US selling-season target date changes
queue-priority behaviour for a micro-account is observed

base.update_signal: the cluster peak window or the US selling-season target shifts

nodes.definition: Name the inverted-duty / GST drag as a cash-cycle cost, not a per-garment COGS add. Acrylic (MMF) inputs are taxed higher than the output, so input tax exceeds output tax and working capital is trapped in slow GST refunds ([FACT]). This bites A2 (the fine-acrylic value driver) specifically, since acrylic is the input whose tax is inverted. The magnitude is [UNKNOWN] and it is a T9 cash-cycle line, not a clean Rs/garment COGS line: inventing a per-garment figure for it would be the exact fabrication the honesty discipline forbids. It is named here and quantified in T9's cash-conversion-cycle math, where it lengthens the cash-out the working-capital trap describes.

excluded: the base cash cycle (its own node)

pros.claim: Classing inverted duty as cash-cycle not COGS prevents a fabricated per-garment add
pros.example: A2's acrylic refund lag lengthens the cash-out without inventing a Rs/garment line

cons.claim: An [UNKNOWN] magnitude routed to T9 limits how much it can shape the launch decision here
cons.example: without the refund-lag size the A2 cash penalty stays directional

failure_modes: adding a fabricated inverted-duty figure to the per-garment COGS stack
ignoring that the drag specifically lengthens A2's cash cycle
acceptance_tests: the inverted-duty drag is stated as a [FACT] mechanism trapping working capital, biting A2, with magnitude [UNKNOWN], expressed as a T9 cash-cycle cost not a per-garment COGS add
revisit_triggers: T9 quantifies the GST refund lag
the MMF input/output tax rates change
the article fibre mix shifts the inverted-duty exposure

base.update_signal: T9 quantifies the refund lag or the MMF tax rates change

nodes.definition: Establish that the same garment has different costs at different volumes and that cost falls in STEPS, not smoothly. Volume cuts cost through two channels, not one: it (a) amortises per-style setup, and (b) clears the dye-lot small-batch surcharge. Both are fixed/threshold effects, so the per-garment cost drops in discrete steps - the first big step is crossing the ~500 kg/colour economic dye MOQ (surcharge gone), the second is amortising setup over a low-thousands run. Three tiers: micro (launch capsule, highest per piece, real cost above the bands), small-batch repeat (a hero style/colour proven, falls toward the bands), and sustained single-program volume (lowest per piece, only if utilisation is genuinely full).

excluded: the dye-MOQ step detail (its own node)
the setup-amortisation step detail (its own node)

pros.claim: Framing cost as stepwise stops a reader assuming a smooth volume discount
pros.example: cost barely moves until the dye-MOQ step, then drops, rather than gliding down per piece

cons.claim: The step locations depend on the same blocked MOQ and setup figures
cons.example: the exact volume where the first step lands moves with the named dye MOQ

failure_modes: modelling a smooth per-piece discount instead of discrete steps
assuming the lowest tier is reached before utilisation is genuinely full
acceptance_tests: the two threshold channels (clear the dye-lot surcharge, amortise setup) are named, the per-garment cost is shown to drop in steps with the dye-MOQ step first, and the three volume tiers are stated
revisit_triggers: the dye-lot economic MOQ is quoted and fixes the first step
the setup amortisation MOQ is quoted
a hero style/colour proves out and reaches a repeat tier

base.update_signal: a dye-MOQ or setup-amortisation figure fixes a step location

nodes.definition: Detail the first and biggest step on the volume cost curve: crossing the dye-house economic MOQ. Below ~500-2,000 kg/colour the dye lot carries the +20-50% small-batch surcharge; once a colour's volume clears that economic MOQ the surcharge disappears, and the per-garment cost steps down for every garment of that colour at once. This is why the first sustained win comes from proving ONE colour to economic-MOQ volume rather than spreading thin across many colours: concentrating volume on a hero colour clears the surcharge step, whereas adding a fourth or fifth colour re-incurs it. The step is a threshold, not a gradient, so partial progress toward it earns nothing.

pros.claim: Isolating the dye-MOQ step shows the cheapest first win is colour concentration
pros.example: proving one hero colour to economic MOQ removes the surcharge for that whole colour at once

cons.claim: Concentrating on one colour trades cost for assortment breadth the brand may need
cons.example: a narrow colour range may underperform on a fashion-led drop even at lower cost

failure_modes: spreading volume across many colours and never clearing the surcharge on any
treating partial progress toward the economic MOQ as if it earned a partial discount
acceptance_tests: the dye economic-MOQ surcharge is stated as the first cost step, with clearing it via a hero colour named and the threshold-not-gradient nature made explicit
revisit_triggers: a named dyer's economic MOQ and surcharge are quoted
a hero colour reaches economic-MOQ volume
the colour plan changes the volume per colour

base.update_signal: a named dyer's economic MOQ/surcharge or a hero-colour volume changes

nodes.definition: Detail the second step on the volume cost curve: amortising per-style setup. Over a 150-piece run the setup uplift is ~+$2-10/garment; over a low-thousands repeat run it falls to ~+$0.30-1.50/garment and effectively vanishes. This step is reached not by adding colours but by REPEATING a proven style at higher volume, so its lever is style depth (re-orders of a winner), distinct from the dye-MOQ step's colour-concentration lever. Together the two steps explain why a small-batch repeat (a hero style/colour proven, low-thousands) falls toward the published conversion bands while the launch capsule sits above them: the repeat clears both thresholds the launch capsule sits below.

included: how the two steps return cost to the bands
excluded: the per-style setup basis (its own node)

pros.claim: Separating the setup step from the dye step shows two distinct levers (style depth vs colour concentration)
pros.example: re-ordering a winning style amortises setup even if its colour already cleared the dye MOQ

cons.claim: Style-depth amortisation assumes the style is a durable winner, which a fashion drop may not be
cons.example: a one-season hit never earns the repeat run that amortises its setup

failure_modes: expecting setup to amortise without a repeat run of the same style
conflating the setup step with the dye step and double-counting the discount
acceptance_tests: the setup-amortisation step is stated with the 150-piece vs low-thousands per-garment spread, the repeat-a-winning-style lever named, and its combination with the dye step shown to return cost toward the bands
revisit_triggers: a winning style earns a repeat run
the per-style setup figure is quoted
the repeat run volume changes the amortisation

base.update_signal: a repeat-run volume or the per-style setup figure changes

nodes.definition: State that the make-vs-buy crossover IS the [UNKNOWN] job-work rate. Owning knitting beats subcontracting only when (owned per-piece cost at your real utilisation) < (subcontract per-piece rate), where owned per-piece = (machine amortisation + programmer + operator + power + maintenance + linker) / pieces actually run. The crossover cannot be located until the subcontract rate is known - the same missing number as the band precision - so volume strategy and the blocker are the same question. The reconstructed-consensus verdict (buy at launch, graduate to owning knitting only at sustained single-program volume, linking LAST because it is both the throughput ceiling and the hardest skill to re-hire, dyehouse and machine-building NEVER) is consistent with the cost view; an adversarial analyst-B sharpened it by noting 'buy' is itself a family (multi-vendor mesh vs single-vertical full-package FOB vs greige+controlled-dye) whose own trade study is blocked by the same [UNKNOWN] rate plus the [UNKNOWN] FOB MOQ.

included: the verdict and the linking-last/never rules
the buy-is-a-family sharpening and its blockers
excluded: the [UNKNOWN] rate's blocker status (its own node)
the launch verdict composition (its own node)

pros.claim: Tying the crossover to the [UNKNOWN] rate shows volume strategy and the blocker are one question
pros.example: the same quote run that tightens the bands also tells whether owning knitting can ever undercut subcontracting

cons.claim: With the rate [UNKNOWN] the crossover is a structure, not a located volume
cons.example: the owned-vs-bought breakeven cannot be placed on the volume axis until the rate is quoted

failure_modes: claiming a make-vs-buy crossover volume without the subcontract rate
owning knitting before sustained single-program utilisation, or owning linking before knitting
acceptance_tests: the crossover is stated as the owned-vs-subcontract per-piece inequality gated by the [UNKNOWN] rate, with buy-at-launch, graduate-on-sustained-volume, linking-last, and dyehouse/machine-never all named
revisit_triggers: the job-work rate quote run lands and locates the crossover
a single program reaches sustained machine-filling volume
a used-machine landed quote changes the owned per-piece math

base.update_signal: the job-work rate or a sustained-volume program changes the crossover

nodes.definition: Define the clean hand-off to T9's landed-cost P&L. Take the per-article conversion bands as the ex-factory input, apply the volume-tier adjustment (small-batch dye surcharge + thin setup amortisation at the brand's actual launch MOQ, i.e. the micro-cost uplift), then hand that adjusted ex-factory figure to T9, which stacks freight + duty (cotton ~16.5% ≈ wool ~16%, with acrylic/MMF ~32% the outlier) + insurance + broker + drayage + financing on top. Ex-factory to landed MULTIPLIES, it does not add a little: duty is a percentage, so it scales with the ex-factory level, which is why A3's premium fibre price compounds at landed and why the acrylic A2 is the article most penalized at the border (32% MMF duty), while A1's cotton core stays the structurally friendliest into the US on its demand/sell-window/repeat-LTV strengths, not on a duty edge over wool. T9 owns whether the venture makes money (contribution margin after CAC); this KB owns only the honest factory-gate number, the volume adjustment, and the cash it ties up.

pros.claim: A clean hand-off prevents the factory-gate number being mistaken for the landed or P&L answer
pros.example: passing the volume-adjusted ex-factory band to T9 keeps duty and CAC where they belong

cons.claim: The hand-off inherits the upstream band and uplift uncertainty
cons.example: a blocked ex-factory band passes its width through to the landed figure

failure_modes: handing T9 the raw conversion band without the volume-tier adjustment
treating duty as an additive line rather than a percentage that scales with ex-factory level
acceptance_tests: the hand-off passes the volume-adjusted ex-factory band to T9, states duty multiplies (scales with the ex-factory level), and assigns the landed/CAC verdict to T9/T7 not this KB
revisit_triggers: T9 changes the landed-stack composition or duty rates
the volume-tier adjustment method changes
a 2025-26 US surcharge alters the duty scaling

base.update_signal: the T9 landed stack, duty rates, or volume-adjustment method changes

nodes.definition: Enforce the binding honesty discipline across every money/capacity/performance/regulation claim: each is tagged [FACT] (cited public source), [ESTIMATE] (method + basis + confidence, carrying the literal word estimate), or [UNKNOWN] (genuinely not known, named as a blocker, never fabricated). Cost/price/throughput/MOQ bands are [ESTIMATE] and never fake-precise; a genuinely-missing number (the Ludhiana per-piece job-work rate) stays [UNKNOWN] and is named as the blocker. No over-promising: there is no magic device, no building our own machine, and AI is a multiplier not a substitute. Off-paper friction/speed-money is described as mechanism, never a named-party accusation, with amounts [UNKNOWN] by design. Coverage is a floor, not a ceiling. This guardrail governs how every sizing, band, cash, and scaling claim in this KB may be expressed.

pros.claim: A single explicit guardrail keeps every downstream figure honest and auditable
pros.example: tagging every MOQ and conversion band [ESTIMATE] and the job-work rate [UNKNOWN] prevents any number reading as a quote

cons.claim: Heavy tagging can make the analysis read as hedged and lower its perceived decisiveness
cons.example: a reader wanting one ex-factory number is given a tagged band plus a named blocker

failure_modes: fabricating a point figure for an [UNKNOWN] number to look decisive
over-promising with a magic device, an own-machine build, or AI as a substitute
acceptance_tests: every money/MOQ/throughput/regulation claim is tagged [FACT], [ESTIMATE] (with method+basis+confidence), or [UNKNOWN] (named as a blocker, never fabricated), with no over-promising and off-paper material kept mechanism-not-accusation
revisit_triggers: a new node introduces a money/MOQ/throughput claim
a public-source [FACT] is added or updated
an [UNKNOWN] is resolved by a quote run and re-tagged [ESTIMATE]

base.update_signal: a new claim is introduced or an [UNKNOWN] is resolved to an [ESTIMATE]

nodes.definition: Produce the launch go/no-go verdict, composing the micro-cost uplift, the first cheque, the working-capital trap, the seasonal timing, the make-vs-buy crossover, and the honesty guardrail into one decision. The merged rule: a launch is a go only when (1) the first cheque (dye-MOQ yarn + setup + conversion + tied cash) fits the cash runway with the working-capital trap priced in, (2) the drop is NOT timed into the Jul-Oct cluster peak, (3) it is planned at 2-4 colours (colour-starved, not style-starved) so the dye-lot MOQ is not over-committed, and (4) it BUYS at launch (subcontract into the mesh or run a B1-vs-B2 trade study) rather than making, since the make-vs-buy crossover is blocked by the [UNKNOWN] rate and utilisation fails at capsule volume. A demand-true product whose first cheque exceeds the runway, or that launches into the peak, is a no-go until the cash plan or timing is fixed.

pros.claim: Composing all reads into one verdict gives an actionable launch/hold call instead of scattered signals
pros.example: the verdict holds a peak-timed, cash-starved launch even when the product itself looks profitable

cons.claim: A single verdict can over-simplify when the cash and timing conditions point opposite ways
cons.example: a product strong enough to fund the cheque may still need to wait out the peak

failure_modes: issuing a go on a profitable unit cost while the first cheque exceeds the runway
launching into the Jul-Oct peak or over-committing the dye lot with too many colours
acceptance_tests: the verdict combines the micro-cost uplift, the first cheque vs runway, the working-capital trap, the seasonal timing, and the buy-at-launch crossover, refusing a peak-timed or cash-starved launch and holding 2-4 colours
revisit_triggers: a first-cheque, cash-runway, or timing input changes
the job-work rate quote run relocates the crossover
the colour plan or capsule scope changes

base.update_signal: a cash, timing, or crossover input to the verdict changes

nodes.definition: Define the loop that keeps the batch, cash, and scaling reads current. A refresh cadence (re-run on each material data acquisition) plus material-change triggers - the job-work + FOB quote run (which collapses the band precision, the make-vs-buy crossover, and the B1-vs-B2 trade study at once), a named dye-lot MOQ and surcharge, a named per-style setup figure, live 2025-26 yarn Rs/kg, an observed ex-factory lead time, a T9 landed-input or duty-rate change, and a cluster-peak-window shift - that send the analysis back through LAUNCH_FIRST_CHEQUE, the conversion bands, and the volume-step curve. The single highest-leverage trigger is the on-the-ground job-work quote run: it converts the whole illustration into a real model. Without this loop the snapshot silently goes stale as the [UNKNOWN] rate stays unquoted and yarn prices drift.

included: re-entry into the first cheque, bands, and step curve

pros.claim: A trigger list with the quote run keeps the lowest-confidence numbers on a path to resolution
pros.example: the quote run fires the loop and replaces the [UNKNOWN] rate, tightening every band at once

cons.claim: Too-frequent refresh churns the reads without new signal, since most inputs update rarely
cons.example: re-running the bands before any quote lands wastes effort on unchanged blockers

failure_modes: no cadence so the snapshot ages while the [UNKNOWN] rate stays unquoted
ignoring a fired trigger (a job-work quote) and continuing on the illustration
acceptance_tests: a refresh cadence and an explicit material-change trigger list exist, each routing back to LAUNCH_FIRST_CHEQUE, the conversion bands, and the volume-step curve, with the job-work quote run named as the highest-leverage trigger
revisit_triggers: a material-change trigger fires
the cadence proves too frequent or too sparse for how the inputs update
the quote run lands and converts the model

base.update_signal: a material-change trigger fires or the cadence is tuned

edge_cases.description: Inverted-duty drag is added as a per-garment COGS line
edge_cases.trigger: a fabricated Rs/garment figure for the GST refund lag is folded into the stack
edge_cases.mitigation: carry inverted-duty as a T9 cash-cycle cost with magnitude [UNKNOWN], biting A2, not a COGS add

edge_cases.description: A smooth per-piece volume discount is modelled instead of discrete steps
edge_cases.trigger: cost is interpolated linearly between volumes rather than at the dye and setup thresholds
edge_cases.mitigation: model the two threshold steps and note partial progress toward a threshold earns nothing

edge_cases.description: Owning knitting is recommended at launch on a hoped-for lower per-piece cost
edge_cases.trigger: an owned-line cost is computed at full utilisation the capsule cannot fill
edge_cases.mitigation: buy at launch; place the crossover only once the [UNKNOWN] rate is quoted and a single program fills the line

edge_cases.description: Launch colours are spread wide and no colour ever clears the dye surcharge
edge_cases.trigger: five or six colours are planned, each below economic dye MOQ
edge_cases.mitigation: hold 2-4 colours and concentrate a hero colour to economic MOQ to clear the surcharge step

edge_cases.description: The ex-factory figure is handed to T9 without the volume-tier adjustment
edge_cases.trigger: the raw conversion band is passed as the landed input at the launch MOQ
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the surcharge + thin-setup uplift at the actual launch MOQ before the hand-off to T9

edge_cases.description: Friction/speed-money is named as a specific party's act or given a rupee amount
edge_cases.trigger: the off-paper mechanism is written as an accusation or a per-garment figure
edge_cases.mitigation: keep it mechanism-not-accusation with amounts [UNKNOWN] by design; it is not a per-garment COGS line

edge_cases.description: The job-work / FOB quote run lands and contradicts the illustrative bands
edge_cases.trigger: real per-piece knit/link rates and an FOB MOQ become available
edge_cases.mitigation: fire the review loop, replace the [UNKNOWN] rate with the quoted [ESTIMATE], tighten the bands, and relocate the crossover

workflow.description: State the model is ex-factory conversion cost and is not landed cost, COGS-to-stock, a P&L, or a live quote
workflow.gate: the four excluded numbers are each named and routed to T9 or T7/T9

workflow.description: Tie yarn to ~50-60% of the stack as the anchored level and the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate to the uncertainty
workflow.gate: yarn share is an [ESTIMATE] from the 54% anchor and the rate is named as the uncertainty with the effort conclusion

workflow.description: Hold the knit+LINK Rs/piece rate [UNKNOWN], bound it with a shape-only study, and state what a quote run unblocks
workflow.gate: the rate is [UNKNOWN] with no public figure, fabrication forbidden, and the quote-run leverage stated

workflow.description: State the ~150-500 kg/colour dye-lot MOQ, convert to sweaters, and conclude 2-4 launch colours
workflow.gate: the dye-lot MOQ is the binding minimum, colour-starved-not-style-starved, as an [ESTIMATE]

workflow.action: Rank the garment/CMT MOQ beneath it
workflow.description: State the ~100-300 pcs/style-colour CMT MOQ as the smaller constraint
workflow.gate: the CMT MOQ is placed beneath the dye lot's 500+-piece-per-colour commitment

workflow.description: Spread sampling/PPS/tech-pack/lab-dip/AQL setup over the MOQ and show the per-garment uplift
workflow.gate: setup is an [ESTIMATE, LOW] spread shown at 150 vs 1,000 pieces with the band-understatement consequence

workflow.description: Give the A1/A2/A3 ex-factory bands as labelled illustrations blocked at the [UNKNOWN] rate
workflow.gate: each band is a labelled [ESTIMATE] with the study shape-only and the knit+LINK lines [UNKNOWN]

workflow.description: Stack setup + dye surcharge to show ~1.3-2x the band midpoint at a 150-piece run
workflow.gate: the uplift is an [ESTIMATE, LOW] multiplier with the MOQ and setup figures named as blockers

workflow.description: Sum dye-MOQ yarn + setup + conversion + tied cash as the runway-sizing number
workflow.gate: the first cheque is a few-lakh-rupee [ESTIMATE, LOW-MED] blocked by the [UNKNOWN] dye MOQ and rate

workflow.action: Foreground the working-capital trap and timing
workflow.description: Carry the first cheque across the ~6-12 week cycle and overlay the Jul-Oct peak rule
workflow.gate: the cash-out is framed as front-loaded with the do-not-launch-into-the-peak rule attached

workflow.description: Show cost falling in steps via the dye-MOQ and setup thresholds across the three tiers
workflow.gate: the two threshold channels and three tiers are named with the dye-MOQ step first

workflow.action: Compose the launch verdict and review loop
workflow.description: Combine micro-cost, first cheque, cash trap, timing, and the buy-at-launch crossover, then set the refresh triggers
workflow.gate: the verdict refuses a peak-timed or cash-starved launch and the loop names the quote run as the highest-leverage trigger

dominance_rules.rule: The honesty guardrail dominates any pressure for a single decisive ex-factory number
dominance_rules.rationale: the knit+LINK rate is [UNKNOWN], so an over-decisive figure would be a fabrication
dominance_rules.trigger: a request for one firm ex-factory cost or a quoted job-work rate
dominance_rules.action: answer only with a labelled [ESTIMATE] band plus the named [UNKNOWN] blocker and the quote-run path

dominance_rules.rule: The dye-lot MOQ dominates the garment/CMT MOQ as the binding minimum
dominance_rules.rationale: the dye lot forces 500+ pieces/colour while the CMT MOQ is only ~100-300
dominance_rules.trigger: the launch is sized on the garment MOQ
dominance_rules.action: bind on the dye-lot MOQ and plan 2-4 colours before sizing styles

dominance_rules.rule: The first cheque dominates the unit cost for sizing the launch
dominance_rules.rationale: the cheque (dye-MOQ yarn + setup + conversion + tied cash) is far larger than any per-garment cost
dominance_rules.trigger: the launch or runway is sized on unit cost x pieces
dominance_rules.action: size on the first-cheque formula carried across the cash cycle

dominance_rules.rule: The micro-volume uplift dominates the published bands at capsule scale
dominance_rules.rationale: setup and the dye surcharge push true cost to ~1.3-2x the band midpoint at 150 pieces
dominance_rules.trigger: a band is quoted as the launch cost
dominance_rules.action: apply the uplift multiplier before reading the band as launch cost

dominance_rules.rule: The working-capital trap dominates a profitable-on-paper unit cost
dominance_rules.rationale: cash gone for months can bankrupt a brand whose unit cost looks fine
dominance_rules.trigger: a go is justified on a profitable ex-factory cost alone
dominance_rules.action: test the first cheque against the runway with the cash cycle priced in before any go

dominance_rules.rule: Buy-at-launch dominates owning a step at capsule volume
dominance_rules.rationale: an owned line is starved of utilisation and the crossover is blocked by the [UNKNOWN] rate
dominance_rules.trigger: owning knitting or linking is proposed at launch
dominance_rules.action: buy/subcontract at launch; graduate to owning only on sustained single-program volume, linking last

dominance_rules.rule: The threshold step curve dominates a smooth volume-discount assumption
dominance_rules.rationale: cost falls at the dye and setup thresholds, not gradually
dominance_rules.trigger: a linear per-piece discount is applied across volumes
dominance_rules.action: model discrete steps and credit no discount for partial progress toward a threshold

dominance_rules.rule: A flagged [UNKNOWN] or low-confidence input dominates a confident downstream conclusion built on it
dominance_rules.rationale: a conclusion cannot be more certain than its weakest load-bearing input
dominance_rules.trigger: the crossover or a band carries a conclusion above its own confidence
dominance_rules.action: cap the conclusion's confidence at that of its weakest input and name the quote-run confirmation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the ex-factory boundary before computing any band or cheque
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building figures that are later re-scoped because landed or P&L numbers crept inside the gate

anti_rework_rules.rule: Hold the knit+LINK rate [UNKNOWN] and label every band an estimate at the moment it is written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later honesty sweep that must re-caveat figures already quoted as facts

anti_rework_rules.rule: Bind on the dye-lot MOQ and set the colour count before sizing styles or the first cheque
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a launch sized on the garment MOQ that must be re-planned once the dye lot forces 500+ pieces/colour

anti_rework_rules.rule: Add the per-style setup and dye-surcharge uplift when the conversion band is built
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a band read as launch cost that must be re-derived once the micro-volume uplift is surfaced

anti_rework_rules.rule: Size the first cheque on the formula and carry it across the cash cycle the first time
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a runway plan built on unit cost that must be redone once the cash-out duration is added

anti_rework_rules.rule: Model the volume curve as discrete steps from the start, not a smooth discount
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a scaling plan that must be reworked once the dye and setup thresholds are placed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Carry inverted-duty and friction as cash-cycle / [UNKNOWN], never as per-garment COGS
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a COGS stack that must be stripped of fabricated lines in a later honesty pass

anti_rework_rules.rule: Name the job-work quote run as the confirmation path on every [UNKNOWN]-blocked figure as it is stated
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later pass to attach the unblocking action to numbers already published without it

iteration_protocol.trigger: the Ludhiana per-piece knit + LINK job-work rate (and an FOB price + MOQ) quote run lands
iteration_protocol.action: replace the [UNKNOWN] rate with a quoted [ESTIMATE], tighten the conversion bands, recompute the first cheque, and relocate the make-vs-buy crossover

iteration_protocol.trigger: a named Ludhiana dyer quotes a real dye-lot MOQ and small-batch surcharge
iteration_protocol.action: re-size the binding minimum, the micro-volume uplift, and the dye-MOQ step

iteration_protocol.trigger: a named unit quotes per-style setup (sampling/PPS, tech-pack, lab dips, AQL)
iteration_protocol.action: re-amortise the setup, update the micro-cost uplift, and re-place the setup step

iteration_protocol.trigger: live 2025-26 yarn Rs/kg per fibre/count becomes available
iteration_protocol.action: update the yarn level in the two-number frame and the conversion bands, and recompute the first cheque

iteration_protocol.trigger: an observed ex-factory lead time or a returns-settlement term changes the cash cycle
iteration_protocol.action: re-frame the working-capital trap and re-test the launch verdict

iteration_protocol.trigger: T9 supplies a landed-input or duty-rate change, or a 2025-26 US surcharge
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the hand-off's volume-adjusted input and the duty-scaling note

iteration_protocol.trigger: the cluster peak window or the US winter selling target shifts
iteration_protocol.action: re-time the launch and re-issue the seasonal go/no-go

iteration_protocol.trigger: a single program reaches sustained machine-filling volume
iteration_protocol.action: re-evaluate the make-vs-buy crossover against the now-known rate, linking last

priority_rationale: The boundary frame, the two-number split, and the [UNKNOWN] rate blocker are foundational because every band, cheque, and crossover reads from them; the binding dye-lot MOQ and the garment/CMT MOQ and per-style setup precede the conversion bands and the micro-volume uplift they push above; the first cheque, working-capital trap, seasonal timing, and inverted-duty drag size the cash before revenue; the volume step curve and its dye and setup steps plus the make-vs-buy crossover describe how cost falls in steps and where owning could win; the honesty guardrail governs every money/MOQ/throughput expression; and the T9 hand-off, the launch go/no-go, and the review loop come last because they pass the adjusted figure to the landed P&L, compose all upstream reads into a launch decision, and keep the lowest-confidence numbers on a path to the unblocking quote run.
